fields: h, intro, items [{t, d, link, label}]. label: the tab's short text ("IQ", "FAT · SAT"); without one the tab shows the stage number.
best_for: BinderTabs files ordered stages as tab dividers in the open qualification binder, each signed off before the next (look `binder-tabs`, steps block).

block.intro: One commissioning and qualification (C&Q) plan covers every stage.

items.d: Flush, pressure test, sanitization, start-up, punch list.
items.label: Commissioning

items.t: Factory and site acceptance tests (FAT and SAT)
items.d: Tested before shipping, then on your utilities.
items.label: FAT · SAT

items.d: Installed as designed: drawings, materials, joints, slopes, instruments.
items.label: IQ

items.d: Operating limits and worst case tested.
items.label: OQ

items.d: Required quality, reproducibly, across the seasons.
items.label: PQ

items.d: Yearly review of data and changes; requalify where they point.
items.label: Review

instances.h: What a Purified Water URS should settle

block.h: What a Purified Water URS should settle
block.intro: Give every requirement a number and one sentence. Suppliers then answer in your numbering, and your evaluators score the same rows.

items.d: Purified Water to USP, Ph. Eur. or both, by edition. Say where the system starts and ends, and what is by others.
items.label: Grade

items.d: List every point of use, washers and humidifiers too. Give peak draw in L/h, daily volume, temperature and planned growth.
items.label: Demand

items.d: Attach feed water analyses from every season, and the coldest feed temperature. Cold feed cuts membrane output.
items.label: Feed

items.t: Quality limits and where you prove them
items.d: Name each limit and its pharmacopoeia. Say where it is measured, online or in the lab, and who sets alert and action levels.
items.label: Limits

items.d: Settle the sanitization method first: it decides the materials. Then write materials as performance, unless a standard names one.
items.label: Sanitize

items.d: Where failed water goes, restart after a power cut, user access, audit trail, data retention and backup, and screen language.
items.label: Controls

items.d: Room size and access, power, air, drains and room temperature. Name who obtains each Canadian approval, such as pressure registration.
items.label: Site

items.d: Who writes and approves each protocol, and whether factory test results count toward qualification. Define acceptance: tests, run length, signatures.
items.label: Tests

items.d: A dated document schedule, the handover set, response hours, spares on site, training hours and the warranty start event.
items.label: Handover

instances.h: Your URS or RFQ, answered line by line

block.h: Your URS or RFQ, answered line by line
block.intro: Send your user requirements specification (URS), request for quotation (RFQ) or tender. It comes back answered in your own numbering.

items.d: Every clause answered where you wrote it. Nothing renumbered, merged or skipped.
items.label: Clauses

items.d: Meets, meets with a note, or differs. A line that does not apply says why.
items.label: Answer

items.d: Each answer names the document and page that shows it.
items.label: Proof

items.d: Every departure from your specification, with its reason. If there is none, the page says "none".
items.label: Departures

items.d: Every field answered, none left blank. Send the form or comparison grid with your RFQ.
items.label: Bid form

items.d: What the answers state can go into your purchase order as written [confirm].
items.label: Contract
